llmlang.cli.find_pyproject.disposition: new entry: moved build.py's CLI logic into the llmlang package as cli.py, as part of packaging this as a real pip-installable tool with a console-script entry point. Previously build.py was explicitly excluded from self-hosting (treated as "just the CLI wrapper"); on reflection that exemption was weaker than the ones used elsewhere (e.g. for one-line private helpers) since this code encodes real, user-facing behavioral contracts - flag-vs-config precedence, what --output-format json's shape actually is, how multiple paths merge into one report. Rather than carry forward an informal, unconfigured exemption, every function here now has either a real handle+entry or an explicit [llm-exempt] marker (_plural, _usage) - the same rule everything else in this codebase already follows. No behavior changed from the pre-move build.py, only usage/help text (build.py -> llmlang) and the leading underscore dropped from functions that now have real entries, reserving it for the two that stayed exempt.
